answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. When an identity double-spends, spams, or fails a verifiable task, peers can submit evidence and slash that bond; honest identities recover theirs after a dispute window. The bond makes a Sybil swarm costly: splitting control across more names requires locking more capital, while one proven fraud can lose funds. A karst survey agent at the wharf might share a task thread, but those names still need separate bonds.
